title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
地之大德曰生在聖人則為仁所以得天
下者也有開於先必傳於後則天下之本
在太子太子正而天下定矣得天下以仁
而教太子以正以仁得之以仁守之以正
教之以正受之世世相承勿替引之
皇明所以垂萬世無疆之休者在是豈惟漢唐
宋不敢企哉雖夏商周亦莫之逮也洪惟
太祖高皇帝龍潛淮右閔元季生靈之塗炭不
得已而起救之入金陵而民皆按堵定元
===
都而市不易肆遂平天下成混一之功史
臣賛之以為雖曰天命人歸要亦
神武不殺之所致也則其得天下以仁固可
見矣
太祖既建儲宫嘗采經傳格言為書名曰儲君
昭鑑錄以訓戒之又
諭宫臣曰汝等講論誦說之時必導之以正
使其道明德立才器充廣庶幾他日克勝重
任則其教太子以正又可見矣
punctuated:
地之大德曰生，在聖人則為仁，所以得天下者也。有開於先，必傳於後，則天下之本在太子，太子正而天下定矣。得天下以仁，而教太子以正，以仁得之，以仁守之，以正教之，以正受之，世世相承，勿替引之。皇明所以垂萬世無疆之休者在是，豈惟漢唐宋不敢企哉？雖夏商周亦莫之逮也。
洪惟太祖高皇帝龍潛淮右，閔元季生靈之塗炭，不得已而起救之。入金陵而民皆按堵，定元都而市不易肆，遂平天下，成混一之功。史臣賛之，以為雖曰天命人歸，要亦神武不殺之所致也，則其得天下以仁固可見矣。
太祖既建儲宫，嘗采經傳格言為書，名曰《儲君昭鑑錄》，以訓戒之。又諭宫臣曰：「汝等講論誦說之時，必導之以正，使其道明德立，才器充廣，庶幾他日克勝重任。」則其教太子以正又可見矣。
translation_en:
…the great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called giving life; in the sage it becomes benevolence, the means by which he gains all under Heaven. What is founded by those who come first must be transmitted to those who follow. Thus the foundation of all under Heaven lies in the crown prince: when the crown prince is upright, all under Heaven is secure. The realm is gained through benevolence, and the crown prince is taught uprightness. Through benevolence it is gained; through benevolence it is preserved. Uprightness is taught, and uprightness is received. Generation succeeds generation, extending the succession without allowing it to lapse. Herein lies the means by which our august Ming bequeaths boundless blessings for ten thousand generations. Is it merely that the Han, Tang, and Song dare not aspire to equal it? Even the Xia, Shang, and Zhou cannot match it.
We reverently reflect that Taizu, the Gao Emperor, while still a hidden dragon in Huaiyou, pitied the people’s desperate suffering in the final years of the Yuan and felt compelled to rise and save them. When he entered Jinling, the people all remained secure in their homes; when he subdued the Yuan capital, the markets continued undisturbed. He then pacified all under Heaven and accomplished its unification. The court historians praised him, holding that, although this could be attributed to Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance, it was ultimately also achieved through his divine martial prowess, which did not resort to killing. Clearly, then, he gained the realm through benevolence.
After Taizu had established the heir apparent, he selected maxims from the classics and their commentaries to compile a book entitled Record of Illustrious Examples for the Crown Prince (Chujun zhaojian lu), using it to instruct and admonish him. He also instructed the officials of the crown prince’s household: “When you lecture, discuss, recite, and explain, you must guide him in uprightness, so that his understanding of the Way becomes clear, his virtue firmly established, and his talents and capacities fully developed. Thus he may one day be capable of bearing his weighty responsibilities.” Clearly, then, he also taught the crown prince uprightness.

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖子神孫繩繩繼繼以仁厚為心法以正儲嗣
為家法而其所以正儲嗣者又各有訓鑑
在焉故
太宗文皇帝嘗取儲君昭鑑錄稍充廣之益以
太祖之謨訓名曰文華寶鑑而
宣宗章皇帝又有御製帝訓二十五篇始於君
德奉天而終於馭夷藥餌
憲宗純皇帝又采諸書格言及
祖宗實訓為書名曰文華大訓凡四卷曰進學
===
養德厚倫明治而各有條目於其間皆所
以教太子者也皆教之以正者也而其所
以為教則又皆本諸當時身所受教者而
出乎躬行心得之餘者也昔漢高帝不事
詩書而手敕其子有勤學習書之語唐太
宗内多慚德而作帝範有飭躬睦親之言
宋真宗矯誣上天而承華要略有清心辨
佞之說所謂夫子教我以正夫子未出於
正者也安得與我
punctuated:
聖子神孫，繩繩繼繼，以仁厚為心法，以正儲嗣為家法，而其所以正儲嗣者，又各有訓鑑在焉。故太宗文皇帝嘗取《儲君昭鑑錄》，稍充廣之，益以太祖之謨訓，名曰《文華寶鑑》。而宣宗章皇帝又有御製《帝訓》二十五篇，始於君德、奉天，而終於馭夷、藥餌。憲宗純皇帝又采諸書格言及祖宗實訓為書，名曰《文華大訓》，凡四卷，曰進學、養德、厚倫、明治，而各有條目於其間，皆所以教太子者也，皆教之以正者也。而其所以為教，則又皆本諸當時身所受教者，而出乎躬行心得之餘者也。
昔漢高帝不事《詩》《書》，而手敕其子有勤學習書之語；唐太宗内多慚德，而作《帝範》，有飭躬睦親之言；宋真宗矯誣上天，而《承華要略》有清心辨佞之說。所謂「夫子教我以正，夫子未出於正」者也。安得與我
translation_en:
His sagely sons and divine grandsons succeeded one another without interruption, taking benevolence and generosity as their guiding principles of mind and the proper formation of the imperial heir as their house rule. Each also possessed instructional mirrors for guiding the heir aright. Thus Emperor Taizong Wen once took the Record of the Heir Apparent’s Illuminating Mirror (Chujun Zhaojian Lu), expanded it somewhat, and supplemented it with Taizu’s counsels and instructions, naming it the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua Baojian). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang also composed twenty-five chapters of Imperial Instructions (Dixun), beginning with “The Ruler’s Virtue” and “Serving Heaven” and ending with “Managing the Foreign Peoples” and “Medicines.” Emperor Xianzong Chun likewise selected maxims from various books and authentic instructions of the imperial ancestors to compile a work entitled Great Instructions of Literary Splendor (Wenhua Daxun). Its four volumes were entitled “Advancing Learning,” “Nurturing Virtue,” “Strengthening Human Relationships,” and “Illuminating Governance,” each with its own constituent topics. All these works served to educate the crown prince; all taught him what was right. Moreover, their teachings were all grounded in the instruction the emperors themselves had received in their day and flowed from what they had personally practiced and inwardly understood.
In former times, Emperor Gao of Han did not devote himself to the Book of Odes or the Book of Documents, yet his handwritten admonition to his son contained words urging diligent study and practice in writing. Taizong of Tang had much shameful conduct in his private life, yet in composing the Model for Emperors (Difan), he spoke of regulating one’s conduct and maintaining harmony with one’s kin. Zhenzong of Song falsely invoked Heaven, yet his Essentials for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua Yaolüe) spoke of purifying the mind and discerning flatterers. These exemplify the saying, “You teach me what is right, yet your own conduct does not proceed from what is right.” How could they be ranked alongside our …

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
朝之訓鑑並稱哉惟昔大禹之克勤克儉而
有典則以貽子孫成湯之不殖不邇而有
風愆以訓蒙士文武有關睢麟趾之化而
以謨烈啓後人所謂其為父子兄弟足法
而後民法之者也是則與我
朝之訓鑑同一揆矣今
天子仁孝之德格于上下篤生
元良以正儲位而其教養之道必遠稽三王
之典謨近遵
===
列聖之訓鑑而内本乎躬行心得之正理所以
為萬世計者至矣然三王之所以教世子
者具載於賈誼書保傅諸篇諄諄以早諭
教與選左右為急或者以為古今異宜而
莫之行然其間有宜於今而不拂乎古者
未始不可行也其曰太子之幼也使仁者
養之孝者繦之賢者傍之及其學也師以
道之教訓傅以傅之德義保以保其身體
其教之也必以孝仁禮義道習之也必□□□
punctuated:
朝之訓鑑並稱哉？惟昔大禹之克勤克儉，而有典則以貽子孫；成湯之不殖不邇，而有風愆以訓蒙士；文武有關睢麟趾之化，而以謨烈啓後人。所謂其為父子兄弟足法，而後民法之者也。是則與我朝之訓鑑同一揆矣。
今天子仁孝之德格于上下，篤生元良以正儲位，而其教養之道，必遠稽三王之典謨，近遵列聖之訓鑑，而内本乎躬行心得之正理，所以為萬世計者至矣。然三王之所以教世子者，具載於賈誼書保傅諸篇，諄諄以早諭教與選左右為急。或者以為古今異宜而莫之行，然其間有宜於今而不拂乎古者，未始不可行也。其曰：「太子之幼也，使仁者養之，孝者繦之，賢者傍之；及其學也，師以道之教訓，傅以傅之德義，保以保其身體。其教之也，必以孝仁禮義；道習之也，必□□□」
translation_en:
…how could these be mentioned alongside the instructive precedents of our dynasty? In antiquity, Yu the Great was diligent and frugal, and left established standards to his descendants. Cheng Tang neither amassed wealth nor approached sensual pleasures, and left admonitions against wayward habits and faults to instruct the uninitiated. Kings Wen and Wu brought about the moral transformation celebrated in “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Feet” (Linzhi), and enlightened later generations through their counsels and achievements. This is what is meant by the saying that only when one’s conduct as father, son, elder brother, and younger brother is worthy of emulation will the people emulate it. These examples thus accord with the instructive precedents of our dynasty.
Now the Son of Heaven’s benevolence and filial devotion reach those above and below. He has been blessed with an excellent heir, securing the position of the heir apparent. In educating and nurturing him, he must look back to the statutes and counsels of the Three Kings and follow the more recent instructive precedents of the sage emperors of our dynasty, grounding all this inwardly in correct principles personally practiced and grasped in his heart. His provision for ten thousand generations is thus consummate. Yet the methods by which the Three Kings educated their heirs are fully recorded in such chapters as “The Protector and the Preceptor” (Baofu) in the writings of Jia Yi. These repeatedly stress the urgency of instruction from an early age and the selection of attendants. Some consider ancient and modern circumstances different and therefore do not put these methods into practice. Nevertheless, those among them that suit the present without conflicting with antiquity can certainly be implemented. The text says: “When the crown prince is an infant, have benevolent people nurture him, filial people swaddle him, and worthy people attend him. When he begins his studies, the Grand Preceptor guides him through instruction, the Grand Mentor inculcates virtue and righteousness in him, and the Grand Guardian safeguards his physical well-being. His instruction must employ filial devotion, benevolence, ritual propriety, and righteousness; in guiding him and forming his habits, one must [three illegible characters]…”

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
詞氣之間衣服器用之具皆有節適以合
矩度又必選天下之端士孝悌博聞有道
者以衛翼之一或有邪人間於其間則必
屏而去之太子朝夕所與居處出入左右
前後無非正人所聞正言所見正事所行
正道而未嘗見一邪行則喻教得左右正
而太子正矣三代有道之長以輔翼太子
有此具也豈獨得天下以仁之效哉今誠
舉而行之則所以端天下之大本者在是
===
矣夫三代得天下以仁我
太祖既與之同而用夏變夷之功則又過之三
代教太子以正今
皇上既用其道而復益以
祖宗之訓鑑則又盡善也將見
國祚靈長本支蕃衍傳之萬世億萬斯年永
永無窮矣豈止如夏商周之傳二三十世
歷七八百年而已哉區區漢唐宋又無足
道矣謹以是為對
punctuated:
詞氣之間、衣服器用之具，皆有節適，以合矩度。又必選天下之端士、孝悌博聞有道者，以衛翼之。一或有邪人間於其間，則必屏而去之。太子朝夕所與居處、出入，左右前後，無非正人；所聞正言，所見正事，所行正道，而未嘗見一邪行，則喻教得、左右正，而太子正矣。三代有道之長，以輔翼太子有此具也，豈獨得天下以仁之效哉？今誠舉而行之，則所以端天下之大本者在是矣。
夫三代得天下以仁，我太祖既與之同，而用夏變夷之功則又過之。三代教太子以正，今皇上既用其道，而復益以祖宗之訓鑑，則又盡善也。將見國祚靈長，本支蕃衍，傳之萬世，億萬斯年，永永無窮矣。豈止如夏商周之傳二三十世、歷七八百年而已哉？區區漢唐宋，又無足道矣。謹以是為對。
translation_en:
…in speech and tone, and in clothing, utensils, and other articles of use, everything is regulated and fitting, conforming to proper standards. Moreover, upright gentlemen from throughout the realm—men who are filial and respectful toward their elder brothers, widely learned, and possessed of the Way—must be selected to protect and assist him. Should even one wicked person enter their midst, he must be excluded and removed. Those with whom the crown prince lives morning and evening, those who accompany him when he goes out or returns, and those to his left and right, before and behind, are without exception upright men. What he hears is upright speech; what he sees is upright conduct; what he practices is the upright Way. Having never witnessed a single wicked deed, he receives proper instruction and has upright attendants, and so becomes upright himself. The long continuance of good government under the Three Dynasties was due to these provisions for assisting the crown prince. Could it have resulted solely from their having gained All under Heaven through benevolence? If these measures are now truly adopted and put into practice, herein lies the means of setting straight the great foundation of All under Heaven.
The Three Dynasties gained All under Heaven through benevolence. Our Taizu equaled them in this, while surpassing them in his achievement of transforming the barbarians through Chinese civilization. The Three Dynasties instructed their crown princes in uprightness. His Majesty now follows their methods and further supplements them with the ancestral emperors’ admonitions and instructive examples, making this instruction perfect in every respect. We shall see the dynasty’s allotted tenure endure, its main line and collateral branches multiply, and its succession continue for ten thousand generations—for hundreds of millions of years, forever without end. How could it be limited to the twenty or thirty generations and seven or eight hundred years of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou? The comparatively insignificant Han, Tang, and Song scarcely merit mention. I respectfully submit this as my answer.

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第二問
喬宗
同考試官教諭林批此策不徒多識前言而其
尚友師古之志固可槩見得士如子蓋所謂傑然者
同考試官教諭林批策塲正欲觀學者之識非
掩其所不知也此卷五策材識不凡而此篇尤見底蘊
京畿之士洽化之深益驗矣
考試官洗馬梁批通閱三塲知非凡士以文字多不能
盡錄錄如是一二以見其餘耳抑吾望子豈止於文字間哉
===
考試官左諭德楊批此策歷舉道統道學之聖賢而旁
及近代君臣之事以別其同異亦一大議論也有士如此而以為世不
我知何哉今既知子矣孔子曰則何以哉勉之勉之
士生千載之下而欲論千載之上惟當求
其道之相若而不必計其位之相同也故
求其道之相若則鄒魯聖賢雖擬之唐虞
三代之君臣而不為妄如但以其位而已
則漢唐宋之君臣豈皆前代聖賢匹哉君
子於此則亦當辨其有近諛與否者矣請
punctuated:
第二問
喬宗

同考試官教諭林批：此策不徒多識前言，而其尚友師古之志，固可槩見。得士如子，蓋所謂傑然者。

同考試官教諭林批：策塲正欲觀學者之識，非掩其所不知也。此卷五策，材識不凡，而此篇尤見底蘊。京畿之士洽化之深，益驗矣。

考試官洗馬梁批：通閱三塲，知非凡士。以文字多，不能盡錄，錄如是一二，以見其餘耳。抑吾望子，豈止於文字間哉！

考試官左諭德楊批：此策歷舉道統道學之聖賢，而旁及近代君臣之事，以別其同異，亦一大議論也。有士如此，而以為世不我知，何哉？今既知子矣。孔子曰：「則何以哉？」勉之，勉之！

士生千載之下，而欲論千載之上，惟當求其道之相若，而不必計其位之相同也。故求其道之相若，則鄒魯聖賢，雖擬之唐虞三代之君臣，而不為妄。如但以其位而已，則漢唐宋之君臣，豈皆前代聖賢匹哉？君子於此，則亦當辨其有近諛與否者矣。請

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
因明問所及而條陳之唐虞三代之時上
有堯舜禹湯文武之君下有皐夔稷契伊
傅周召之臣精一執中之相授也建中建
極之相傳也見知聞知之相承也道統之
盛治化之隆曠萬世而莫及矣後世乃有
儗其君臣者何哉宰我稱夫子賢於堯舜
蓋以事功言之堯舜治天下夫子又推其
道以教萬世也朱子謂顏子優於湯武蓋
以德言之湯武微有粗迹顏子渾渾無痕
===
迹也曾子易簀之事程子謂其惟求得正
而不慮死與武王行一不義而得天下不
為者同心孟子距楊墨之說程子謂其以
道拯人心之溺與禹稷以身救世者同功
是一聖三賢者其道同乎唐虞三代之君
者也儗之固其倫矣豈可以時位言哉賈
山稱漢文帝將興堯舜之道三王之功唐
史臣賛太宗除隋之亂比跡湯武宋太祖
洞開殿門之言朱子謂其心與堯舜之心
punctuated:
因明問所及而條陳之。唐虞三代之時，上有堯舜禹湯文武之君，下有皐夔稷契伊傅周召之臣，精一執中之相授也，建中建極之相傳也，見知聞知之相承也。道統之盛，治化之隆，曠萬世而莫及矣。後世乃有儗其君臣者，何哉？宰我稱夫子賢於堯舜，蓋以事功言之，堯舜治天下，夫子又推其道以教萬世也。朱子謂顏子優於湯武，蓋以德言之，湯武微有粗迹，顏子渾渾無痕迹也。曾子易簀之事，程子謂其惟求得正而不慮死，與武王行一不義而得天下不為者同心。孟子距楊墨之說，程子謂其以道拯人心之溺，與禹稷以身救世者同功。是一聖三賢者，其道同乎唐虞三代之君者也，儗之固其倫矣，豈可以時位言哉？

賈山稱漢文帝將興堯舜之道、三王之功，唐史臣賛太宗除隋之亂，比跡湯武。宋太祖洞開殿門之言，朱子謂其心與堯舜之心
translation_en:
…set these matters out point by point in response to your enlightened question. In the age of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, above were such rulers as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; below were such ministers as Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. They handed down the teaching of refinement and single-mindedness in holding fast to the Mean; they transmitted the establishment of the Mean and the supreme standard; and they succeeded one another in understanding, whether through seeing or through hearing. The flourishing of the succession of the Way and the grandeur of government and moral transformation were unequalled throughout the ages. Why, then, have people in later ages compared others to these rulers and ministers?

Zai Wo declared that the Master surpassed Yao and Shun in worth. This was speaking in terms of achievement: Yao and Shun governed the world, while the Master further extended their Way to teach all subsequent ages. Master Zhu said that Master Yan surpassed Tang and Wu. This was speaking in terms of virtue: Tang and Wu retained slight traces of roughness, whereas Master Yan was wholly integrated, leaving no such traces. Concerning Master Zeng’s replacement of his sleeping mat, Master Cheng said that he sought only to attain what was right, without worrying about death, and thus shared the resolve of King Wu, who would not commit a single unrighteous act even to gain the world. Concerning Mengzi’s rejection of the doctrines of Yang Zhu and Mo Di, Master Cheng said that he used the Way to rescue people’s drowning hearts, and thus matched the achievement of Yu and Ji, who personally labored to save the world. This one sage and these three worthies shared the Way of the rulers of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Comparing them is therefore to compare those of the same kind. How could one judge merely by their era and position?

Jia Shan declared that Emperor Wen of Han would revive the Way of Yao and Shun and the achievements of the Three Kings. The historians of the Tang praised Taizong for ending the disorder of the Sui, comparing his deeds to those of Tang and Wu. Regarding the words of Taizu of Song about throwing open the palace hall’s doors, Master Zhu said that his heart and the hearts of Yao and Shun…

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
合宋神宗勵精為治之初王安石稱其欲
追堯舜三代不難是四君者其位同乎唐
虞三代之君者也儗之若近諛矣然亦人
臣尊君之常耳至於劉向稱董仲舒有王
佐之才雖伊呂無以過蘇軾稱諸葛亮出
師二表與伊訓說命相表裏魏徵對唐太
宗以稷契臯陶為良臣而願為之石介以
范仲淹富弼為一夔一契而又責弼以行
伊周之事是數臣者其位與唐虞三代之
===
臣同者也儗之若妄矣盖亦賛美嚮慕之
意耳有稱天民之先覺如伊尹者元祐宰
臣薦程子入講筵之語也有以淑問如臯
陶為比者熙寧執政使張子厚按獄而言
之也宋理宗追封朱子稱其傳孔孟之學
抱伊傅之才朱子賛張敬夫有卜其見伊
呂而失蕭曹之語此四儒者其道與唐虞
三代之臣同者也儗之亦其倫矣豈以勢
分言哉孟子曰人皆可以為堯舜荀卿曰
punctuated:
合。宋神宗勵精為治之初，王安石稱其欲追堯舜三代不難。是四君者，其位同乎唐虞三代之君者也，儗之若近諛矣，然亦人臣尊君之常耳。至於劉向稱董仲舒有王佐之才，雖伊呂無以過；蘇軾稱諸葛亮出師二表與伊訓說命相表裏；魏徵對唐太宗，以稷契臯陶為良臣而願為之；石介以范仲淹、富弼為一夔一契，而又責弼以行伊周之事。是數臣者，其位與唐虞三代之臣同者也，儗之若妄矣，盖亦賛美嚮慕之意耳。
有稱天民之先覺如伊尹者，元祐宰臣薦程子入講筵之語也；有以淑問如臯陶為比者，熙寧執政使張子厚按獄而言之也。宋理宗追封朱子，稱其傳孔孟之學，抱伊傅之才；朱子賛張敬夫，有卜其見伊呂而失蕭曹之語。此四儒者，其道與唐虞三代之臣同者也，儗之亦其倫矣，豈以勢分言哉？孟子曰：「人皆可以為堯舜。」荀卿曰：
translation_en:
…accorded with theirs. When Emperor Shenzong of the Song first applied himself diligently to governing, Wang Anshi said that it would not be difficult for him to emulate Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties. These four rulers held positions equivalent to those of the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Comparing them may seem close to flattery, yet this is also the customary way in which ministers honor their sovereigns. As for Liu Xiang, he praised Dong Zhongshu as possessing the ability to assist a true king, saying that even Yi Yin and Lü Shang could not surpass him. Su Shi said that Zhuge Liang’s two Memorials on Dispatching the Army complemented the Instruction of Yi and the Charge to Yue. Wei Zheng, in answering Emperor Taizong of the Tang, held up Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao as worthy ministers and wished to be like them. Shi Jie regarded Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi as a Kui and a Xie respectively, and further charged Fu Bi with carrying out the work of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. These several ministers held positions equivalent to those of the ministers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Comparing them may seem unwarranted, but the intention was simply to express praise and admiration.
The description of someone as, like Yi Yin, one of Heaven’s people who first attained understanding comes from the words with which the chief councillors of the Yuanyou era recommended Master Cheng for service at the imperial lectures. The comparison of someone’s good reputation to that of Gao Yao was made when the chief ministers of the Xining era sent Zhang Zihou to investigate a judicial case. In posthumously ennobling Master Zhu, Emperor Lizong of the Song praised him for transmitting the learning of Confucius and Mencius and possessing the talents of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. In praising Zhang Jingfu, Master Zhu spoke of “divining that in him one would find Yi Yin and Lü Shang, but miss Xiao He and Cao Can” [?]. These four Confucian scholars followed the same Way as the ministers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Comparing them thus places them among their proper peers. How could this be a matter of power and rank? Mengzi said, “Everyone can become a Yao or a Shun.” Xun Qing said: …

title: 弘治五年順天府鄉試錄
text:
塗之人可以為禹公明儀曰文王我師也
則唐虞三代之君臣以鄒魯聖賢與漢唐
宋之君臣諸儒儗之亦不為過但有其道
者不能得其位有其位者不能盡其道此
其治效所以無所見也豈儗之者皆諛且
妄哉使孔子得堯舜之位則顏曾孟子俱
可為皐夔稷契矣使漢有禹湯之君則董
仲舒諸葛亮亦可以為伊傅矣使宋有文
武之君則范仲淹與程張朱子皆可以為
===
周呂矣何患治效之不如古哉雖然世無
孔子焉別顏回愚嘗志伊尹之所志學顏
子之所學以上師孔子今逢
堯舜在位亦欲接武皐夔以備百執事之用也
而世莫我知知之者其在於今為文章之
司命人物之衡鑑者乎尚無以為諛且妄
而麾之幸甚
第三問
劉烶
punctuated:
「塗之人可以為禹。」公明儀曰：「文王我師也。」則唐虞三代之君臣，以鄒魯聖賢與漢唐宋之君臣諸儒儗之，亦不為過。但有其道者不能得其位，有其位者不能盡其道，此其治效所以無所見也。豈儗之者皆諛且妄哉？使孔子得堯舜之位，則顏曾孟子俱可為皐夔稷契矣；使漢有禹湯之君，則董仲舒諸葛亮亦可以為伊傅矣；使宋有文武之君，則范仲淹與程張朱子皆可以為周呂矣。何患治效之不如古哉？雖然，世無孔子，焉別顏回？愚嘗志伊尹之所志，學顏子之所學，以上師孔子。今逢堯舜在位，亦欲接武皐夔，以備百執事之用也。而世莫我知，知之者其在於今為文章之司命、人物之衡鑑者乎？尚無以為諛且妄而麾之，幸甚。

第三問

劉烶
translation_en:
…“An ordinary person on the road can become a Yu.” Gongming Yi said: “King Wen is my teacher.” Thus it is no exaggeration to compare the sages and worthies of Zou and Lu, and the rulers, ministers, and Confucian scholars of the Han, Tang, and Song, to the rulers and ministers of the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. It is simply that those who possessed their Way could not attain their positions, while those who held their positions could not fully realize their Way. This is why no results of their governance were manifest. Surely those who make such comparisons are not all flattering and reckless?

Had Confucius attained the position of Yao and Shun, Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, and Mencius could all have become counterparts of Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Xie. Had the Han possessed rulers like Yu and Tang, Dong Zhongshu and Zhuge Liang could likewise have become counterparts of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Had the Song possessed rulers like Kings Wen and Wu, Fan Zhongyan and Masters Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu could all have become counterparts of the Duke of Zhou and Lü Shang. Why then worry that the results of their governance would fall short of antiquity?

Nevertheless, without a Confucius in the world, how could a Yan Hui be recognized? In my humble way, I have long aspired to what Yi Yin aspired to and studied what Master Yan studied, thereby taking Confucius as my highest teacher. Now that I encounter a Yao or Shun upon the throne, I too wish to follow in the footsteps of Gao Yao and Kui, making myself available for service among the many officials. Yet no one in the world knows me. Might those who recognize me be the men who now preside over the fortunes of literary composition and serve as the arbiters of human talent? I would be most fortunate if they would not dismiss me as flattering and reckless.

Third Question

Liu Ting 劉烶
